---
title: "Errata"
subtitle: "Coppock, A. (2019). Generalizing from Survey Experiments Conducted on Mechanical Turk: A Replication Approach. *Political Science Research and Methods* 7(3), 613-628."
format:
  pdf:
    output-file: coppock_2019a_errata.pdf
    geometry: margin=1.1in
    colorlinks: true
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false

The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2019a> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24168306>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r setup}
library(here)
library(tidyverse)

here::i_am("errata.qmd")

# Corrected values are computed here, at render time, from the maintained pipeline's
# committed output. Published values are read from the extraction of the article, never
# typed into this document.
published_claims <- read_csv(
  here("ground_truth", "published_claims.csv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character(), value_paper = col_character())
)

paper <- function(id) {
  value <- published_claims$value_paper[published_claims$claim_id == id]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

power <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_4_power_simulation.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
table_2 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_2_ri_heterogeneity.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)

power_at <- function(sd) {
  value <- power$power[power$n_per_arm == 500 & power$sd_tau == sd]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

power_02 <- power_at(0.2)
power_01 <- power_at(0.1)
arm_for_08 <- min(power$n_per_arm[power$sd_tau == 0.2 & power$power >= 0.8])

gfk_sig <- table_2$n_sig[table_2$sample == "gfk"]
gfk_tests <- table_2$n_comparisons[table_2$sample == "gfk"]

mt_tests <- as.numeric(paper("t2_mt_n_comparisons"))
mt_expected_02 <- round(mt_tests * power_02)
mt_expected_01 <- round(mt_tests * power_01)

# The treatment the next published sentence names (Hiscox 2006) as the only one to reject
# in more than one sample.
ri <- read_rds(here("maintained", "output", "ri_results.rds"))
rejects <- ri |> filter(max_pval <= 0.05)
in_two <- rejects |> count(study, condition_names, dv) |> filter(n > 1)
stopifnot(nrow(in_two) == 1, in_two$study == "free_trade")
hiscox <- rejects |> semi_join(in_two, by = c("study", "condition_names", "dv"))
stopifnot(setequal(hiscox$sample, c("gfk", "mt")))
original_reject <- rejects |> filter(sample == "original")
stopifnot(nrow(original_reject) == 1, original_reject$study != "free_trade")
p_text <- function(x) if (x < 0.01) "p < 0.01" else str_c("p = ", two(x))

one <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
two <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)

# What the deposit's own output prints, read from the ground truth rather than typed.
gt_all <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "coppock_2019a_ground_truth.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)
deposit <- function(id) {
  value <- gt_all$value_script[gt_all$claim_id == id]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  value
}

# Dependent variables per study grouping, as the deposit's own analysis groups them.
dvs_per_study <- ri |> distinct(study, dv) |> count(study)
n_groupings <- nrow(dvs_per_study)
max_dvs <- max(dvs_per_study$n)
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from this tibble into
# this document and into the machine-readable errata_entries.csv written at the bottom of
# the file, which is what any other document carrying these corrections reads. Before the
# spine existed an entry was written out in prose wherever it was needed, and the copies
# had already diverged.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be set by any of them.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: entries are ordered by severity block (quantity;
# description, interpretation, definition; label, float, cross_reference; wording, spelling,
# typography; bibliographic), discovery order inside a block, and a finding that lands in an
# earlier block renumbers the entries after it. Renumbered 2026-11-07; the old-to-new map is
# in that day's commit message.
#
# The published values come from the extraction of the article and the corrected ones from
# the pipeline, and both stay computed: the fields are built with str_glue() so the numbers
# are produced when this document renders, not typed.
#
# claim_ids is the semicolon-separated list of ground-truth claim_id values the entry
# corrects, and it is what makes "is this finding published?" a query rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where an entry has no ground-truth row, which is normal for a
# bibliographic or structural entry. ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R refuses to build if
# any id here is absent from the ground truth.
#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. The sentence already holds
# it, but only inside prose a reader has to parse. maintained/in_text_claims.R asserts that
# the value it computes for a corrected claim is this one, which is the check that the
# correction this note publishes is the correction the pipeline currently supports. Each
# value comes from the same expression that glues the sentence, so the two cannot be written
# apart, and the gate below re-checks that each one is still inside the span it belongs to.
# An entry of a class that changes no quantity carries NA.
entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "Simulated power, page 622",
  "p. 622",
  str_glue("The MTurk versions of the experiments studied here typically employ 500 subjects per treatment arm, suggesting that we would be well powered (power $\\approx$ [[{paper('fig4_power_at_02')}]]) to detect treatment effect heterogeneity on the scale of 0.2 SD, and moderately powered for 0.1 SD (power $\\approx$ [[{paper('fig4_power_at_01')}]])."),
  str_glue("The MTurk versions of the experiments studied here typically employ 500 subjects per treatment arm, suggesting that we would be [[moderately]] well powered (power $\\approx$ [[{one(power_02)}]]) to detect treatment effect heterogeneity on the scale of 0.2 SD, and [[poorly]] powered for 0.1 SD (power $\\approx$ [[{two(power_01)}]])."),
  str_glue(
    "The simulation results the article deposits, and which Figure 4 is drawn from, give a ",
    "rejection probability of {two(power_02)} at 0.2 SD and {two(power_01)} at 0.1 SD, both ",
    "at 500 subjects per treatment arm. Figure 4 draws guide lines at 500 subjects and at ",
    "power 0.8 and annotates the 0.2 SD curve where it crosses the second of them, which the ",
    "simulation puts at {arm_for_08} subjects per arm rather than 500; the sentence reads the ",
    "height of the guide line rather than the curve. At those rejection probabilities the ",
    "test is moderately well powered at 0.2 SD rather than well powered, and poorly powered at ",
    "0.1 SD rather than moderately so, and both descriptions are corrected with the numbers. The figure itself is correct and is not reprinted here."),
  "fig4_power_at_02;fig4_power_at_01",
  str_c(one(power_02), ";", two(power_01)),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "Significant heterogeneity tests on the TESS/GfK sample, page 622",
  "p. 622",
  str_glue("On the TESS/GfK replications, [[{paper('text_gfk_n_sig')}]] of {paper('text_gfk_n_comparisons')} tests were significant."),
  str_glue("On the TESS/GfK replications, [[{gfk_sig}]] of {gfk_tests} tests were significant."),
  str_glue(
    "The deposited output file for Table 2 records {gfk_sig} significant TESS/GfK test, and ",
    "so does the maintained pipeline; the count does not move with the change R 3.6.0 made to ",
    "`sample()`, which moves the other two rows of that column. Table 2 prints ",
    "{paper('t2_gfk_n_sig')} in the TESS/GfK row of its N Significant column and ",
    "{paper('t2_original_n_sig')} in the Original row, which is that column read in the row ",
    "order of the deposited output file rather than in the table's own; the two entries are ",
    "interchanged. Entry 6 sets out the transposition, and because correcting the table ",
    "requires the pre-R-3.6.0 sampler it is carried there as a note rather than reprinted ",
    "corrected. The corrected count is what makes the ",
    "next sentence true: it says that only Hiscox (2006) returned a significant test in more ",
    "than one sample, which the printed 0 rules out, because the Original sample's single ",
    "significant test is a different study. The one TESS/GfK rejection is Hiscox's negative ",
    "treatment ({p_text(hiscox$max_pval[hiscox$sample == 'gfk'])}), which also rejects on ",
    "MTurk ({p_text(hiscox$max_pval[hiscox$sample == 'mt'])})."),
  "text_gfk_n_sig",
  as.character(gfk_sig),

  3, "definition", "reading", "full",
  "The condition stated for the Holm correction, footnote 8, page 623",
  "p. 623",
  "Identify the smallest p-value for which the following condition holds: [[$p_k \\le \\frac{k}{m}\\alpha$]], where $k$ indexes the p-values, and $\\alpha$ the target significance level.",
  "Identify the smallest p-value for which the following condition holds: [[$p_k > \\alpha/(m - k + 1)$]], where $k$ indexes the p-values, and $\\alpha$ the target significance level.",
  str_c(
    "The condition the note prints is the Benjamini-Hochberg threshold on the false discovery ",
    "rate, not the Holm threshold on the family-wise error rate that the note names and that ",
    "the analysis used. The rest of the note is already Holm's step-down rule: it says to find ",
    "the SMALLEST p-value meeting the condition and to treat it and every larger p-value as ",
    "insignificant, which is where Holm stops and is not how Benjamini-Hochberg is read. So ",
    "the single defect is the condition, and correcting it makes the note describe the ",
    "procedure the code ran. Both scripts call `p.adjust(max_pval, \"holm\")`, the deposit's ",
    "own `coppock_generalizability_ri_analysis.R` and the maintained ",
    "`table_2_ri_heterogeneity.R`, so Table 2's N Significant (Holm) column and every number ",

  NA_character_,
  NA_character_,

  4, "wording", "pipeline", "full",
  "The description of statistical power, page 623",
  "p. 623",
  "Because we are [[relatively]] well powered to detect politically meaningful differences in treatment response, I conclude from this evidence that the treatment effect homogeneity explanation of the correspondence across experimental sites is plausible.",
  "Because we are [[moderately]] well powered to detect politically meaningful differences in treatment response, I conclude from this evidence that the treatment effect homogeneity explanation of the correspondence across experimental sites is plausible.",
  str_glue(
    "The sentence rests on the power figures of entry 1. At the corrected rejection ",
    "probabilities, {two(power_02)} at 0.2 SD and {two(power_01)} at 0.1 SD, the tests are ",
    "moderately well powered rather than relatively well powered, which is the description ",
    "entry 1 now gives them. The conclusion the sentence draws survives on narrower ",
    "evidence: with {mt_tests} MTurk tests at 500 subjects per arm, heterogeneity of 0.2 SD in ",
    "every treatment would produce about {mt_expected_02} rejections against the ",
    "{paper('t2_mt_n_sig')} observed, but heterogeneity of 0.1 SD would produce about ",
    "{mt_expected_01}, so the tests rule out the first and not the second."),
  NA_character_,
  NA_character_,

  5, "wording", "reading", "full",
  "The word naming the procedure in footnote 8, page 623",
  "p. 623",
  "To implement the [[correlation]], order the $m$ uncorrected p-values within a \"family\" from smallest to largest.",
  "To implement the [[correction]], order the $m$ uncorrected p-values within a \"family\" from smallest to largest.",
  str_c(
    "The note is about the Holm correction, which its own first sentence names twice, and ",
    "the sentence that says how to apply it calls it a correlation. Nothing in the analysis ",
    "turns on the word."),
  NA_character_,
  NA_character_,

  # Entries 6 to 8 are notes (decision 15). Each quotes a passage the edition reprints as
  # published and sets no corrected side.
  #
  # Entry 6 is a note and not a correction because the corrected cells, 2 and 9 and 1 in the
  # published row order, are what the deposit prints but not what any run on current R
  # produces: the maintained pipeline returns 1 and 8 and 1, and only the retired
  # pre-R-3.6.0 sampler recovers the deposit (README, "Table 2 in full"; notes.md, the
  # 2026-08-19 entry). A corrected table would print numbers this edition cannot regenerate.
  6, "float", "pipeline", "note",
  "The N Significant column of Table 2, page 622",
  "p. 622, Table 2",
  str_c(
    "Original, N Comparisons {paper('t2_original_n_comparisons')}, N Significant [[{paper('t2_original_n_sig')}]], N Significant (Holm) {paper('t2_original_n_sig_holm')}\n\n",
    "Mechanical Turk, N Comparisons {paper('t2_mt_n_comparisons')}, N Significant {paper('t2_mt_n_sig')}, N Significant (Holm) {paper('t2_mt_n_sig_holm')}\n\n",
    "TESS/GfK, N Comparisons {paper('t2_gfk_n_comparisons')}, N Significant [[{paper('t2_gfk_n_sig')}]], N Significant (Holm) {paper('t2_gfk_n_sig_holm')}") |>
    str_glue(),
  NA_character_,
  str_glue(
    "Table 2 sets its rows in the order Original, Mechanical Turk, TESS/GfK, with ",
    "{paper('t2_original_n_comparisons')}, {paper('t2_mt_n_comparisons')}, and ",

    "reordered to the table's own row order and the N Significant column was not, so the ",
    "Original and TESS/GfK cells of that column are interchanged: in the published row order ",
    "the deposit gives {deposit('t2_original_n_sig')}, {deposit('t2_mt_n_sig')}, and ",
    "{deposit('t2_gfk_n_sig')}. The Holm column, {paper('t2_original_n_sig_holm')}, ",

    "of constant effects in a small minority of comparisons."),
  "t2_original_n_sig;t2_gfk_n_sig",
  NA_character_,

  # Entry 7 is a note and not a correction because the text's 1 and 8 are the counts a strict

  # decide which rule the sentence meant, which is the authors' to say (README, "Table 2 in

  7, "quantity", "pipeline", "note",
  "The Original and Mechanical Turk counts in the sentence reporting Table 2, page 622",
  "p. 622",
  str_glue("Among the original {paper('text_original_studies')} studies, just [[{paper('text_original_n_sig')}]] of the {paper('text_original_n_comparisons')} treatment versus control comparisons revealed evidence of effect heterogeneity. Among the MTurk replications, [[{paper('text_mt_n_sig')}]] of {paper('text_mt_n_comparisons')} treatments were shown to have heterogeneous effects."),
  NA_character_,
  str_glue(

  NA_character_,

  # studies named are the ones notes.md identifies as carrying more than two.
  8, "description", "pipeline", "note",
  "The limit of two dependent variables per study, page 618",
  "p. 618",
  "I limited the number of dependent variables analyzed in each study to [[two]].",
  NA_character_,
  str_glue(
    "The deposit's analysis groups the data into {n_groupings} studies, and the largest of ",
    "them carries {max_dvs} dependent variables: Johnston and Ballard (`expert_economists`) carries ",

) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values),
                as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and
# its spans outnumber its values.
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# An entry that changes a quantity has to say which one, and an entry that changes none may
# not carry a value. The class is the declaration and this is where it binds.
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | !is.na(entries$claim_ids))
)
# form == "note" declares that the entry quotes a passage and proposes no change to it, so it
# has no corrected side. The two have to agree: a note carrying corrected text would print a
# correction this edition does not make, and a correction carrying NA would print "NA" where
# its corrected sentence belongs.
stopifnot(is.na(entries$corrected) == (entries$form == "note"))

# Every id an entry claims to correct must be a real ground-truth claim. The build gate in
# ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R checks the same property from the other side; checking it
# here too means a dangling id cannot survive a render.
gt_ids <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "coppock_2019a_ground_truth.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)$claim_id
cited_ids <- entries$claim_ids |>
  str_split(";") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_trim() |>
  discard(\(x) is.na(x) | x == "")
stopifnot(all(cited_ids %in% gt_ids))

# The prose below counts the entries in words, as the note has always done.
# The count of corrections only: a note is not a correction, and the opening sentence counts
# corrections.
number_word <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine",
                 "ten", "eleven", "twelve")
n_entries_word <- number_word[sum(entries$form != "note")]
n_notes_word <- number_word[sum(entries$form == "note")]

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

`r str_to_sentence(n_entries_word)` sentences in the published article need correcting. Two state numbers the deposited replication archive does not support, and a third describes the tests' statistical power more generously than the corrected numbers allow. The remaining two are in the footnote that explains the Holm correction: one calls the correction a correlation, and the other states the Benjamini-Hochberg threshold on the false discovery rate in place of the Holm threshold the footnote names and the code applied. All `r n_entries_word` are in the section reporting the randomization inference tests of treatment effect homogeneity. It also carries `r n_notes_word` entries of a second kind, which quote a passage and propose no change to it: the Original and TESS/GfK cells of Table 2's N Significant column, which are interchanged; the Original and Mechanical Turk counts in the sentence that reports the table, which differ from the deposit by one each; and the sentence limiting each study to two dependent variables, which is true or false according to what counts as a study. **No correction and no note here changes a conclusion of the paper.** The tests still reject the null of constant effects in a small minority of comparisons, the counts in Table 2 come from the code rather than from the footnote's formula, and the correspondence between the Mechanical Turk and probability sample estimates is untouched.

Article DOI: [10.1017/psrm.2018.10](https://doi.org/10.1017/psrm.2018.10). Replication archive: [10.7910/DVN/F1CFFM](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/F1CFFM). The code behind every corrected value below is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/coppock_2019a>, and every one of them is recomputed when this document is rendered rather than typed into it.

Corrections are marked in **bold**. Numbers the article hedges with an approximation sign keep the article's own precision, because the approximation is the claim; fuller values appear in the note beneath each entry.

```{r render-entries, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every emitted entry opens
# with one. A field holding two passages keeps them one paragraph apart.
emit_entry <- function(i) {
  e <- entries[i, ]
  cat("\n\n# ", e$entry, ". ", e$title,
      "\n\n**Published.** \"", bold(e$published), "\"", sep = "")
  # A note entry has no corrected side, and that absence is the whole of the form: an empty
  # Corrected block would read as a correction to nothing.
  if (e$form != "note") cat("\n\n**Corrected.** \"", bold(e$corrected), "\"", sep = "")
  cat("\n\n*", e$note, "*\n", sep = "")
}
walk(which(entries$form != "note"), emit_entry)
```

# Carried, and not corrected

The `r n_notes_word` entries below are different in kind from the `r n_entries_word` corrections in this note. Each quotes a passage this edition reprints exactly as the paper published it, and proposes no change to it.

Two of them concern the counts of significant homogeneity tests, which come back only under a sampler R retired in 3.6.0, so that any corrected figure would be one the maintained pipeline cannot regenerate, or which turn on a choice of inequality that is the author's to make. The third is a sentence about the study's design that is true under one count of studies and false under another. Correcting any of the three would mean either printing a number this edition cannot reproduce or writing the author's prose for him.

Each is recorded here because an edition that silently reproduced them would leave a reader unable to tell a faithful reprint from an uncorrected error.

```{r entries-carried, results="asis"}
walk(which(entries$form == "note"), emit_entry)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else that
# carries these corrections reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot drift.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
